scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: The WAN uplink between Router1 and Router0 (Router1’s eth2 interface carrying 10.10.0.2/8) is down, which also breaks the RIP adjacency on that link.
- Mechanism: IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) hosts send traffic to their default gateway (Router0). Router0 must forward off-net via next-hop 10.10.0.2 on eth2, but with the far end (Router1 eth2) down, ARP to 10.10.0.2 fails and Router0 returns “Destination Host Unreachable” to IT/CS senders. From the other side, Router1 has no routes to 192.168.1.0/24 or 192.168.2.0/24 and returns “Destination Net Unreachable” when those subnets are the destination.
- Localization: Router1 eth2 on the wan_r0_r1 link. Evidence: Router1 ip addr shows “eth2 … state DOWN … inet 10.10.0.2/8”. Router1’s routing table lacks 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, only has connected 192.168.3.0/24 and 192.168.4.0/24. Pings corroborate: it_lab1→1.0.0.5 gets “From 192.168.1.1 Destination Host Unreachable”; office_pc→it_lab1 gets “From 192.168.3.1 Destination Net Unreachable”.
- Root cause: Router1’s eth2 interface (to Router0) is down/unplugged or administratively disabled, breaking the R0–R1 WAN.
- Corrective fix: Bring Router1 eth2 up (e.g., ip link set dev eth2 up) and ensure RIP is enabled on eth2. Verify link state on both ends, ARP to 10.10.0.2 from Router0, and that Router1 re-learns 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24. Afterward, IT/CS reachability outside their departments will be restored. Note: TPO (192.168.3.5) to Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) currently works via Router1↔Router2; earlier reports likely predated this check.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies the router0–router1 WAN link 10.10.0.0/8 and Router1 eth2 as the affected interface.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states IT and CS are the only impacted subnets while TPO/other networks remain reachable (notably TPO→128.168.0.x), matching the required symptom distinction.
The agent explicitly recommends bringing up Router1's eth2 (ip link set dev eth2 up) and ensuring RIP runs on it, which matches the expected remediation.

The agent ran relevant reachability and host-config checks; ping outputs show Router0 returning 'Host Unreachable' for IT/CS, Router1 returning 'Net Unreachable' for off-net, and host config was fetched showing router1's eth2 down — together these observations justify the WAN-link-down conclusion. Some specific internal details (e.g., ARP failure, RIP timers) are plausible and consistent but are inferred rather than directly printed in full route/ARP outputs in the log.
